hints: Focus on how an ester splits in acid hydrolysis, the carbonyl side becomes the carboxylic acid and the O-alkyl side becomes the alcohol.
Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, so look for an ester whose C=O carbon is attached to an ethyl group ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$).
Split each ester at the single C-O bond and add -OH to the carbonyl part to see which one rebuilds propanoic acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall acid hydrolysis of esters**

Think of an ester as acid part + alcohol part joined together. With dilute acid and water it splits back apart.

$$\text{RCOOR' + H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{RCOOH + R'OH}$$

**Identify what we need for propanoic acid**

Propanoic acid has 3 carbons with the structure $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. That means the R group on the carbonyl carbon must be ethyl, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$.

$$\text{needed ester = CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOR'}$$

**Check the carbonyl side of each option**

Look only left of the C=O first. Option A has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C=O}$, which is exactly the propanoyl fragment. On hydrolysis it gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ plus ethanol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH + CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

options.A: This is ethyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The acyl part is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO-}$, so acid hydrolysis adds water across the ester link to give propanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ and ethanol.
options.B: This is ethyl 2-methylpropanoate, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Its carbonyl carbon is attached to a branched propyl group, so hydrolysis gives 2-methylpropanoic acid, not propanoic acid. Trap is ignoring the branch on the acid side.
options.C: This is propyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Its carbonyl side is only $\text{CH}_3-$, so hydrolysis gives ethanoic acid plus propan-1-ol. Trap is confusing the alcohol propyl group with the acid propanoic part.
options.D: This is ethyl butanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Its carbonyl side has one extra carbon, so hydrolysis gives butanoic acid with 4 carbons, not propanoic acid with 3 carbons.
